answer_1.quote: The field of MT Quality Estimation (QE) emerged, aiming to develop models that can approximate the quality of machine-generated translations ... We work with the recently published multilingual QE dataset MLQE-PE, allowing us to test the generalisability of our approaches across different languages and quality scores.
answer_1.outputs: quality scores (Direct Assessment, HTER) for machine-translated sentences

answer_2.quote: In QE, the best practice is to use Pearson's r to measure performance ... Column MSE is the average mean squared error.

answer_4.quote: For each language, 9000 sentence pairs (7000 train, 1000 dev, 1000 test) were annotated on two different scales: Human-targeted Translation Edit Rate (HTER) ... Direct Assessment Scores (DA): Each sentence pair was judged on a scale from 0-100 by at least 3 evaluators. ... One of the authors, a German native speaker, manually annotated translations in the test set that are grammatically correct but do not preserve the meaning of the source.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators were instructed to assign a DA score below 70 to inadequate translations; HTER was computed as the averaged edit rate after post‑editing.
